one_line: Chahamana (Chauhan) king of Ajmer and poet-king who founded a Sarasvati temple and Sanskrit college, inscribing his own drama on stone.

appearance.age_look: Early 30s, lean but well-built warrior-scholar with a straight, upright posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with sharp jawline, medium wheatish complexion, straight prominent nose, neatly trimmed moustache that turns slightly upward, small close-cropped beard along the jaw, calm but intense eyes with a thoughtful default expression that softens into a slight confident smile.
appearance.hair: Glossy black hair tied in a neat low knot at the back of the head, mostly hidden under a simple gold-rimmed conical turban-like cloth crown (mukuta) in deep maroon with a narrow gold band at the base and a single small white feather at the front left.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate 12th-century north Indian royal outfit: a long, knee-length angarakha-style wrap tunic in rich deep maroon with subtle woven floral motifs in darker tone, fastened on the right with visible gold cord ties; over it a sleeveless fitted coat (kancuka) in muted gold with narrow vertical maroon borders, slightly flared at the hips; a broad cloth belt in dark indigo with fine gold edging wraps the waist; lower body in straight, slightly tapered churidar-style trousers in off-white; feet in brown leather strap sandals with simple metal studs; over one shoulder a lightweight pale cream cotton uttariya drape with a thin maroon border, often flowing from left shoulder to right hip; jewellery restricted to a medium-width gold torque necklace, a single thin gold armlet on the right upper arm with a tiny lotus motif, simple circular gold earrings close to the earlobe, and a plain signet ring on his right hand; fabrics look like fine cotton and light silk, appropriate to Rajasthan’s climate, with no excessive ornament but a refined royal elegance.
appearance.signature: A rolled palm-leaf manuscript bound with a red cord held in his left hand, and at his left hip a sheathed straight double-edged sword with a simple steel blade, a plain slightly-curved crossguard and a brown leather scabbard with a narrow maroon strap, the manuscript always more foregrounded than the sword.

ref_desc: Vigraharaja IV appears as a lean early-30s wheatish-complexioned warrior-scholar with oval face, small beard, black hair in a low knot under a maroon gold-rimmed conical cloth crown, wearing a deep maroon angarakha, muted gold sleeveless coat, off-white churidar, dark indigo belt, cream uttariya, minimal gold jewellery, and carrying a rolled palm-leaf manuscript with a plain brown-sheathed sword at his hip in a deep maroon, muted gold, off-white, dark indigo and brown palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character of Vigraharaja IV as a dignified 12th-century north Indian warrior-scholar king: a lean early-30s man with wheatish complexion, oval face, straight nose, neatly trimmed upward moustache and small close-cropped beard, calm intense eyes and a thoughtful default expression with a faint confident smile. His black hair is tied in a low knot, mostly hidden by a simple conical cloth crown like a turban cap in deep maroon with a narrow gold band at the base and a single small white feather on the front left. He wears a knee-length deep maroon angarakha-style wrap tunic with subtle darker floral motifs, fastened on the right with gold cord ties, under a sleeveless fitted muted gold coat that flares slightly at the hips and has narrow vertical maroon borders. A dark indigo cloth belt with fine gold edging wraps his waist over the coat. His lower body has straight, slightly tapered off-white churidar-style trousers, and his feet are in brown leather strap sandals with small metal studs. A pale cream cotton uttariya with a thin maroon border drapes from his left shoulder across his torso and flows to the right hip. Jewellery is modest: a medium-width gold torque necklace, a single thin gold armlet with a tiny lotus motif on his right upper arm, simple circular gold earrings close to the lobe, and a plain signet ring on his right hand. In his left hand he prominently holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a red cord, while at his left hip hangs a sheathed straight double-edged sword with a plain steel blade, slightly curved crossguard and a brown leather scabbard on a narrow maroon strap; the manuscript should visually read as his primary symbol. Use a rich but restrained palette of deep maroon, muted gold, off-white, dark indigo and brown, with clear, clean lines so this exact face, hair, costume and weapons can be redrawn consistently from multiple angles.
